description: Table of names outside effects and handlers that the rule "a subpackage's public API is only effects and handlers" allowed name by name (read by tests/test_public_api_known_violations.py). Violations and boundaries live in the known-violations table tests/data/public_api_known_violations.json; allowed names are placed only in this table (ADR-DOE-API-001 R12).

1 row = 1 allowed name: package (a dir under packages/), module (the module that exports the name), name, group, basis. The key (package, module, name) is the same as an inventory row; rows are sorted by key and do not overlap. Do not place the same key as the violations table.

group = one of the allowed groups whose shape the inventory verifies (the test's ALLOWED_GROUPS). Today there are 12: "Allowed — program helper" (ADR-DOE-API-001 R18 — a function that returns a program, wraps no handler inside, and answers no effect), "Allowed — Hy macro" (R14, R15, R31 — Hy macro names, and rows of public submodules that export only Hy macros), "Allowed — CLI command" (R7, R23, R24, R27, R31, R33 — rows of the console scripts and Rust executables that an ADR rule names; the pairing of name and rule is the test's ADR_COMMANDS), "Allowed — conversion function" (R35 — a function that takes values and returns a value, creates no effect, handler or program inside, and reads no clock, environment, file, process or randomness), "Allowed — ADR-writing function" (R14 — a function exported by a Hy macro module), "Allowed — effect answer type" (R2 — the answer type of a package's effect: the T of EffectBase[T] or the type shown in defeffect's :answer; the bus events that a waiting effect, which answers with a type the body names, declares in its own __doeff_bus_events__; and the types in the answer class's fields, its child classes, and type aliases that list only answer classes — the inventory's answer_types), "Allowed — exception type" (R2 — a child class of BaseException defined by that package), "Allowed — effect value type" (R2 — a class or type alias that appears, type arguments included, in the annotation of a field of an effect class that the same package exposes; fields of value types defined by the package are followed too — the inventory's value_types), "Allowed — pytest plugin registration" (R10, R33 — the pytest11 entry point row, and the names exported by the module that entry point loads), "Allowed — startup entry" (R36 — the name that the .pth shipped by a package calls at every startup of the venv's Python), "Allowed — program-shape builder and type" (R37 — a function that returns a value of a class the package exposes, creates no effect, handler or program inside, and reads no clock, environment, file, process or randomness; plus the class the group's builders return), and "Allowed — handler setting type" (R2 — a type defined by that package that appears, type arguments included, in the annotations of handlers, handler classes and factory arguments that the same package exposes; fields of setting types defined by the package are followed too — the inventory's settings). The test marks red any name whose inventory shape does not fit its group. A group that does not verify the shape cannot be placed.

basis = the ADR rule that allows the row (ADR-DOE-API-001 R<number>), or, for a row without a rule, one English sentence giving the reason it is allowed (one line ending with a period). Do not write record ids or issue numbers. This table can grow with a basis (unlike the violations table, which only shrinks). The test marks a row without a basis red.

A row whose name was moved from a submodule to the entry point is read as the same row without rewriting the table's module, as in the violations table. A name that is in the table but not in the inventory is red — remove fixed names and hidden submodule names from the table (the former move tool finish removes the rows of the children it hid).

Grounds of the current rows (rules of ADR-DOE-API-001): sequence and try_call of doeff-traverse are R18; closing_links of doeff-core-effects and validate of doeff-validation, of the same shape, are also R18; the 155 names (271 rows) used by an outside repo or by another doeff package are R25; the macro modules of doeff-events and doeff-domain, their 2 macro names, and the doeff-hy CLI doeff-hy-check are R31; the public macro module doeff_cluster.macros of doeff-cluster and defsystem are R15 (placed directly under the root when the shared section was hidden in _shared); epoch_ms_of of doeff-time is R35; the 129 exception types thrown by effects and handlers (247 rows over 16 packages — the former known-violations group "Boundary — exception type") are R2; the 108 effect value types (323 rows — 95 names with 298 rows of the former group "Boundary — effect value type" plus 25 rows of "added names") are also R2; the 197 effect answer types (604 rows over 10 packages — 603 rows of the former group "Boundary — effect result type" plus SymbolInfo of doeff-indexer in "added names") are also R2; the former group "Boundary — CLI" and the 9 CLI commands of "added names" are the rules that name them (R7 for doeff-flow; R23 for doeff-linter; R24 for doeff-effects; R27 for doeff-indexer; R33 for doeff-adr); the pytest11 registration and 2 declarations of doeff-hy-pytest are R10; the pytest11 registration of doeff-adr is R33; install of doeff_hy_bytecode_guard is R36. The 3 builder names and 2 type names of doeff-stream (5 rows) are R37. The 13 effect answer types (22 rows) and 2 value types (Message of doeff-llm and Urgency of doeff-notify, 2 rows — the former group "Violation — annotate the effect field or move inside") of the small 14 packages are also R2 (the effect now states its answer type or field type and appears in the inventory); the 65 handler setting types (115 rows over 18 packages — 112 rows of the former group "Boundary — handler setting type" plus 3 rows of "added names") are also R2. SecretManagerClient of doeff-google-secret-manager (the type of the client argument of production_handlers — the former known-violations group "Violation — move into a handler") is also R2.
